articles.title: At least eight killed in Yemen air raids on Houthi-held Hodeidah
articles.summary: Yemen’s government forces face setbacks, struggling to counter Houthi advances despite Saudi air support.
articles.body:
Air raids have targeted Houthi-held areas of Yemen, with at least eight people killed in an air raid in Hodeidah.

Health officials in the Houthi-run capital, Sanaa, said eight people were killed and 17 injured in the targeting of a telecommunications facility in the Red Sea port of Hodeidah on Monday. Houthi-affiliated media later reported 10 deaths and more than 20 injured in the strike.

Anis al-Asbahi, spokesman for the Sanaa-based Ministry of Health and Environment, said efforts were under way to rescue people trapped under the rubble.

A supply depot in Sanaa, held by the Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God) – since September 2014, was also targeted on Monday, with air raids reported in Taiz, Marib, al-Bayda and Saada governorates.

It follows an escalation in cross-border strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis. The Houthis said they had targeted energy and military installations in Saudi Arabia on Sunday. Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced the interception of missile attacks near Riyadh and the kingdom’s western region but did not comment on Houthi claims of strikes.

This follows continued fighting between forces aligned with the internationally recognised Yemeni government and the Houthis, as intense clashes continue around the besieged city of Taiz.

Reporting from Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said Hodeidah has “strategic” value for Yemen’s economy, with more than 90 percent of imported goods entering via the port.

“Saudi Arabia claims to attack assets of the Houthi group that are being used to smuggle ballistic missiles that are being used to target Saudi Aramco oil assets in the heart of Saudi Arabia,” he said.

The war broke out in Yemen in 2014 following the Houthis’ capture of Sanaa and the intervention of a Saudi-led coalition in March 2015 to support government forces, with the rebels regularly targeting Saudi cities with rockets and drones. It largely halted under a 2022 United Nations-brokered truce.

However, intense fighting broke out again in July after Sanaa airport was targeted by Yemeni government forces, when a Houthi delegation was due to land. Since then, Houthi forces have managed to capture the whole Red Sea coast and have advanced towards the government’s interim capital, Aden.

Saudi Arabia has been targeted in near-daily Houthi rocket and drone strikes since then, with one attack on King Khalid international airport in Riyadh in October killing 13 people .

But Wolfgang Pusztai, a defence analyst, said Saudi Arabia could sustain Houthi attacks on its soil for an extended period of time.

“They will not run out of resources, their number of casualties in the war is low, and the Houthi missile and drone attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia are unlikely to break their will,” Pusztai told Al Jazeera.

Yemeni government forces, however, have suffered a series of serious setbacks on the battlefield since they launched their open-ended counteroffensive against the Houthis in October, known as the Dawn of Yemen operation .

“They are under heavy pressure and are currently regrouping to shorten their lines of defence and concentrate on key areas, such as the wider capital region, Taiz, and the northern Marib area,” Pusztai said.

Despite these setbacks, a Houthi offensive to take Aden is unlikely. “[The Houthis] would face a very bloody urban warfare scenario as soon as they would reach the city itself,” he said.

Approximately two million people remain trapped in Taiz, a city still held by government forces but now completely encircled by the Houthis.

Al Jazeera’s Maha Ali, reporting from Taiz, said government forces were still working to repel Houthi attacks across front lines surrounding the city.

Before the siege, approximately 600,000 people in Taiz were completely reliant on humanitarian aid, but there has only been a trickle of aid entering the city in recent weeks.

“It is true that small quantities of some food products and consumer goods are still arriving, but the volume of supplies has fallen very significantly,” said Abdulwahab Alaug, a Yemeni political analyst and academic with Taiz University.

“Food prices have risen dramatically because the flow of food supplies has stopped, or almost come to a complete halt.”

On Sunday, governorate authorities reported that a paramedic was killed and six people were wounded when a Houthi projectile hit an ambulance carrying injured civilians.

The day prior, the Taiz Centre for Rights warned that attacks on ambulances and health facilities were pushing the city’s health system towards collapse, threatening to transform treatable illnesses and life-saving conditions into causes of death.

SAM Organisation for Rights and Freedom reported that 80 civilians have been killed in Taiz and 147 injured in gunfire or shelling in the past 20 days. It also warned that 532 cases of measles, including four deaths, have been recorded since August.

articles.title: Delhi AQI stays poor for ninth day in a row
articles.summary: Delhi AQI stayed “poor” for 9th straight day at 260; winds helped dispersion, but air may turn “very poor” by Thursday as temperatures dip below 10°C.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi, with an AQI of 260 Monday, saw the ninth consecutive poor air day.The city is likely to inhale very poor by Thursday.The minimum temperature is likely to dip below 10 degrees Celsius for the first time this season on Nov 25.Officials said that due to favourable weather conditions, such as strong winds, better ventilation and the missing winter chill at this time of the year, the pollutants dispersed. The low contribution of stubble burning and restrictions introduced by Delhi govt under the winter framework have also helped in reducing emissions.“Westerly winds with speed reaching 10-15 kmph blew over Delhi in the last 24 hours,” a Met official said Monday. Winds below 5 kmph cause pollutants to gather in the air. As average wind speed stayed around 10-15 kmph, that has prevented further deterioration of the air quality.Central Pollution Control Board’s data shows that in Nov so far, the city has recorded 12 very poor days and 11 poor days. The AQI has stayed in the range of 200-300 from Sept 15 onwards. However, it is predicted to turn very poor by Thursday, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi.Several stations in Delhi have already recorded very poor air quality. IGNOU in Maidan Garhi (356), Sirifort (349), Pusa (344), NSUT Jaffarpur (333), Sri Aurobindo Marg (332), Talkatora Garden (324), CRRI Mathura Road (330), ITO (322), North Campus at DU (321), IIT Delhi (308), Ayanagar (307), Burari Crossing (310) and Commonwealth Sports Complex (304) were among the stations that recorded very poor air quality.Secondary organic aerosols at 26.6% remained a dominant source of pollution between 1am and 9am Monday, according to the real-time source apportionment data of the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).It was followed by biomass burning, including stubble burning, domestic solid biofuel, dung cakes and wood, at 21.5%, waste burning (municipal/plastic-rubber containing/e-waste) at 20.3% and secondary inorganic aerosols at 16.6%.The night temperature is likely to dip to 9 degrees Celsius by Wednesday. “Easterly winds prevailed over the city in the past three days and wind direction changed to westerly and north-westerly. As cold and dry westerly winds from western Himalayan region are expected to blow over the next few days, the minimum temperature is expected to dip in the next two days,” another Met official said.The minimum temperature Monday stood at 11.1 degrees Celsius. It was 11.8 degrees Celsius Sunday. It is likely to remain around 11-13 degrees Celsius Tuesday.The maximum temperature was recorded at 26.5 degrees Celsius, which is near normal for this time of the year.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: As tech outages mount, some New Yorkers prepare for the worst
articles.summary: As digital disruptions raise concerns about essential services, some residents are preparing for prolonged outages.
articles.body:
New York City, New York – When a series of technology outages struck services across the United States this month, Kristyn Lavery began thinking about what might happen if the disruptions lasted longer.

The 67-year-old retired fashion designer, who has lived in Manhattan’s East Village since 1981, started keeping cash and extra water in her 32.5-square-metre (350-square-foot) apartment. She also looked into ways to keep warm but says she cannot afford a generator, which can cost hundreds of dollars.

Lavery is part of a trend of US citizens stocking up on essential supplies over fears that the technology outages could presage other vulnerabilities — or even a tech collapse.

Public concern began to grow on November 13, after a malfunctioning flight communication system led to a nationwide halt to air travel. Experts later credited the ground stop to a tech update gone awry.

The flight delays happened around the same time that the tech giant Microsoft announced problems with its services, including the email platform Outlook.

In the following days, the US National Security Agency , the tech company Apple and banks including JPMorgan Chase all reported service disruptions.

Last week, authorities said they were also investigating a suspected hack of the National Crime Information Center and the US Department of Agriculture.

While there is no evidence that the episodes are connected, residents like Lavery say they are worried.

For Lavery, the recent outages have heightened fears shaped by major events like the attacks on September 11, 2001, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Now, with US officials warning about further disruptions, she is determined to take the possibility of another emergency more seriously.

“I feel vulnerable. And I don’t want to be a victim. Yet I feel like, if this happens, it will be on me for not preparing,” she told Al Jazeera.

She remembers what happened in 2012, when flooding from Hurricane Sandy disrupted transport and power in parts of Manhattan. Her neighbourhood went without heat and hot water for days, and residents had to rely on one another.

“I got no help from the government,” Lavery said. “It was neighbours helping neighbours.”

The growing interest in emergency preparedness has become a trend on social media in recent weeks.

On TikTok, a New Yorker, identified only as Nat, posted a video on Tuesday showing the canned food and water she stocked up on for her Lower Manhattan apartment.

“There’s some weird s*** going down in the US. And we don’t really know what’s going on, but I’ve been convinced to stock up,” she said. “I’d rather be crazy than sorry.”

Moderators of Reddit’s r/preppers community — an emergency preparedness forum — said on Sunday that the group had gained nearly 12,000 members in the past month. It recorded 4.2 million views over the same period, up by 2.4 million from the previous month.

There are also signs of increased emergency spending in recent months, even before the tech outages began. Sales from the wholesale retailer Costco, for instance, rose 8.1 percent in October, excluding fuel.

Analysts at Mizuho Securities, a financial firm, estimated that the company’s growth accelerated to about 12 percent in the final week of the month and continued into early November.

They attributed some of the increase to emergency-preparedness purchases due to what they called “apocalyptic concerns” on social media.

Separately, sales of water-purification tablets rose 154 percent and disinfecting wipes 72 percent in the four weeks ending November 1, compared with a year earlier, according to Circana data.

Joel Smernoff, CEO of the New York-based emergency-preparedness company Black Umbrella, told Al Jazeera that his sales had nearly doubled over the past two weeks, largely from new customers.

He explained that the recent outages have made the vulnerabilities of everyday infrastructure feel more tangible.

“It’s the drumbeat of every day: Another huge brand is going down,” Smernoff said.

He also brought up New York’s experience with Hurricane Sandy. After the storm struck, his apartment building near Union Square lost power and running water for six days.

He said older residents on upper floors who could not manage the stairs needed the building superintendent to bring them bottled water.

“We don’t know where or when an unexpected event is going to hit, whether it’s a storm, a cyberattack or infrastructure going down,” Smernoff said. “The rapidity and the frequency of it can be surprising.”

Cybersecurity experts have pointed out that artificial intelligence has made it easier to discover potential flaws in software, forcing companies to proactively seek out and patch vulnerabilities.

But emergency updates can themselves introduce disruptions when they are rolled out across complex systems.

Faced with public questions about the outages, US officials have emphasised they have found no evidence that the recent incidents are part of a coordinated attack.

President Donald Trump himself has tried to allay fears in his recent media appearances.

“Tell them to relax. Everything is good. These are individual events,” Trump told Fox News on Thursday when asked about the outages and whether the public should be preparing for emergencies.

Local officials have also addressed the outages by highlighting government emergency planning. New York Governor Kathy Hochul and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, for example, addressed the disruptions on November 17.

Hochul said she had been receiving daily briefings from state intelligence and cybersecurity teams since the first Microsoft Outlook problems. The state, she explained, had also taken steps to strengthen critical infrastructure.

When asked about the possibility of a wider technological outage affecting utilities, phones and street lights, Mamdani said the city had assigned specific agencies to be responsible for preparing for large-scale disruptions.

In general, New York City Emergency Management advises residents to make an emergency plan and gather supplies for a home kit that can last seven days.

The agency also encourages residents to build an emergency support network and check on neighbours who may be isolated, including older people and those with medical or access needs.

But the succession of outages has prompted some New Yorkers to reconsider how much they rely on technology systems that can suddenly become unavailable.

“I’m in a quandary,” Lavery said. “I tell myself hopefully this is just a fluke. But I feel like we’re not being told what this really is.”

articles.title: I'm angry my Jehovah's Witness mum died - she didn't want to 'disobey God'
articles.summary: Estera Pawlak's mother Ela refused potentially life-saving surgery due to her religious beliefs.
articles.body:
When Estera Pawlak's mother Ela was diagnosed with stomach cancer, she was offered potentially life-saving surgery to remove the tumour.

But the Jehovah's Witness refused as it could have involved a blood transfusion - a procedure that was forbidden in the religion until earlier this year.

Ela had chemotherapy in her native Poland but nothing could keep the disease at bay and she died in Aberdeen in 2024, aged 63.

Estera said the rule change on blood transfusions by the Jehovah's Witnesses made her angry.

"My mum could still be alive," she said. "They took her away from my siblings, my kids, my nieces and nephews.

"She missed out on so much of her life because of something that wasn't actually true."

Estera, now 30, was brought up as a Jehovah's Witness in Aberdeen but moved away from the religion as she grew older.

Her mum moved from Scotland to Świecie in Poland in December 2022 to look after her elderly mother and within months was diagnosed with stomach cancer.

She refused surgery and made inquiries with the religious organisation about alternative treatments - but Estera said she never got an answer.

In the meantime, the symptoms of the cancer began to take hold.

Estera told BBC Scotland: "It should have just been an easy operation to remove part of her stomach.

"The Jehovah's Witness council gave her no plan to move forward, so my mum kept refusing care and became more and more unwell.

"I went to see her three months after the diagnosis and she was in a palliative care ward. It was crazy, I questioned, 'why are you here?'

"She was still so full of life and the most optimistic person you could ever meet. I couldn't understand that she was now dying."

Over the next 12 months, Ela had chemotherapy and medication to boost her red blood cells but it was not enough to keep the disease at bay.

"Even with the chemo and other medications we tried, we were back to square one - mum still needed the operation and a blood transfusion," Estera said.

"At this point it became heartbreaking. She was refusing care and the operation. It felt like mum was giving up, like we weren't good enough.

"But the way she explained it to us was choosing the operation would be like cheating on God. In her faith she felt like she had a relationship with him and couldn't let him down.

"Mum was terrified, she had so much life in her and she wanted to live, but she also said she wouldn't be able to live with herself if she disobeyed God."

After a year of palliative care in Poland, Ela moved back to Scotland in January 2024.

Hours after landing she was rushed to hospital because her condition had deteriorated. She died 10 months later.

In March 2026, Jehovah's Witnesses updated their policy on blood transfusions to allow members to have their own blood removed, stored, and "given back" in medical procedures.

In September, they changed the policy to allow component transfusion. This allows the transfusion of plasma, red blood cells, and platelets.

The transfusion of whole blood is still not allowed.

When she learned about the change in rules, Estera said she had never felt anger like it. She thought it was insulting to everyone who had lost a loved one due to the rule in the past.

"I was in shock for a long time, I couldn't believe it was real. Then the anger came."

She added that thinking about the last months of her mother's life "just breaks me to pieces".

Dileep Lobo, a professor of gastrointestinal surgery at the University of Nottingham who has co-authored papers on treating Jehovah's Witness patients, said the blood policy update was a "game changer" and will save many lives.

"It will save a lot of lives and give us a lot more options for treating people," he said.

"A lot more operations will go ahead because of the rule change."

And he confirmed that without surgery to remove a tumour, treatment for stage two gastric cancer would become palliative.

"So, it may prolong life and improve the quality, but it isn't a cure and without the surgery ultimately the disease will progress and the patient dies," he said.

Andrew Basoo, the national spokesman for Jehovah's Witnesses, said the organisation was "saddened" when they heard someone had lost a loved one in death.

He said "They deserve to be heard respectfully and compassionately.

"Questions about their loved one's treatment warrant careful consideration of the medical evidence and that person's expressed wishes.

"However, since we are unable to fully investigate the situation, it wouldn't be appropriate to comment."

articles.title: BRK muda conta de água no TO e orienta clientes para evitar golpes | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo modelo reorganiza informações sobre consumo, cobrança e tributos. Concessionária afirma que não identificou casos de falsificação de faturas impressas e orienta consumidores a conferir os dados.
articles.summary: Novo modelo reorganiza informações sobre consumo, cobrança e tributos. Concessionária afirma que não identificou casos de falsificação de faturas impressas.
articles.body:
A mudança no visual das contas de água da BRK | Saneatins, implementada no início de novembro, gerou dúvidas entre consumidores sobre a autenticidade dos boletos. A concessionária afirmou que não identificou casos de falsificação de faturas impressas e orientou os clientes a conferir os dados antes de realizar o pagamento.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Segundo a concessionária, a mudança foi feita para atender às exigências da Reforma Tributária. O novo modelo apresenta informações sobre consumo, cobrança e tributos de forma reorganizada.

A empresa informou ainda que os clientes podem utilizar os canais oficiais para confirmar a autenticidade das faturas em caso de dúvidas.

A Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP) foi procurada pelo g1 para informar se há registros de denúncias envolvendo possíveis golpes com contas de água, mas não respondeu até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Conta da água da concessionária BRK Ambiental — Foto: Divulgação/BRK Ambiental

A concessionária orienta os consumidores a conferir o nome completo do titular, o CPF ou CNPJ, o endereço do imóvel e número da ligação, identificado como CDC.

O novo modelo pode apresentar, na parte superior, um dos seguintes títulos: “Documento Auxiliar da Nota Fiscal”, “Aviso de Retenção de Fatura” ou “Aviso de Débito”.

A BRK também recomenda que os clientes priorizem os canais oficiais para consultar e pagar as contas, como o aplicativo Minha BRK, o site da concessionária ou a fatura física entregue pelos leituristas.

Outra orientação é desconfiar de cobranças enviadas por canais não oficiais. A empresa afirma que não solicita alterações de dados bancários nem pagamentos por mensagens de aplicativos ou redes sociais.

Antes de confirmar qualquer transação, o consumidor deve conferir os dados do recebedor exibidos pelo banco ou aplicativo de pagamento.

Para consultar as faturas e acessar outros serviços, os clientes podem utilizar o aplicativo Minha BRK ou acessar o site minhabrk.com.br . A concessionária também atende pelo telefone 0800 644 0195 e pelo WhatsApp (11) 99988-0001.

A empresa informou ainda que passou a exigir cadastro com login e senha para permitir o acesso às faturas digitais pelo site.

Mari Silva é integrante do programa de estágio entre a Rede Anhanguera e Universidade Federal do Tocantins (UFT), sob supervisão de Patrício Reis.

articles.title: Voo de aviões militares russos causa alerta na Coreia do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Seul afirmou que 5 aeronaves russas entraram na zona de defesa aérea do país. Espaço aéreo sul-coreano não foi violado, mas governo emitiu alerta para moradores buscarem abrigo. Moscou alegou que bombardeiros estratégicos Tu-160 realizavam voo sobre Mar do Japão.
articles.summary: Seul afirmou que 5 aeronaves russas entraram na zona de defesa aérea do país. Espaço aéreo sul-coreano não foi violado, mas governo emitiu alerta para moradores buscarem abrigo. Moscou alegou que bombardeiros estratégicos Tu-160 realizavam voo sobre Mar do Japão.
articles.body:
Bombardeiros estratégicos russos entraram na zona de identificação de defesa aérea da Coreia do Sul , informou nesta terça-feira (24) a agência de notícias sul-coreana Yonhap, após corrigir uma informação anterior segundo a qual uma suposta aeronave norte-coreana havia violado o espaço aéreo do país. A Rússia falou em voo programado.

"Cinco aviões militares russos, e não norte-coreanos, penetraram na Zona de Identificação de Defesa Aérea da Coreia do Sul (KADIZ) sobre o Mar do Leste (também conhecido como Mar do Japão)", informou a Yonhap citando o capitão Jang Do-young, porta-voz das Forças Armadas sul-coreanas.

Do-young afirmou que as aeronaves russas se aproximaram da ilha de Ulleungdo, na costa leste do país, em "um possível sinal de incursão no espaço aéreo territorial sul-coreano ".

O incidente fez com que o Ministério do Interior sul-coreano enviasse um alerta aos moradores da ilha, que receberam a orientação de buscar abrigo. O aviso foi suspenso cinco minutos depois, segundo a Yonhap.

"Emitimos preventivamente um alerta para garantir a segurança da população, já que uma possível incursão parecia iminente", disse Do-young.

Aeronave Blackjack (Tu-160), da força nuclear estratégica da Rússia. — Foto: Reprodução/Tupolev

Uma zona de identificação de defesa aérea não constitui espaço aéreo soberano, mas sim uma área na qual os países exigem que aeronaves estrangeiras se identifiquem por razões de segurança. Em geral, espera-se que aeronaves militares notifiquem o país correspondente antes de entrar nessa zona, embora não haja obrigação legal para isso.

O Exército sul-coreano explicou posteriormente que o espaço aéreo do país não foi violado. No entanto, um avião russo "voou até o limite do nosso espaço aéreo", acrescentou o Ministério da Defesa. A pasta informou também que mobilizou caças para escoltar as aeronaves russas durante o incidente e que convocará o representante de defesa russo em Seul como forma de repúdio.

O Ministério da Defesa russo afirmou nesta terça que os bombardeiros estratégicos Tu-160 fizeram um voo programado sobre o Mar do Japão que durou cerca de 10 horas. Agências estatais russas afirmaram que a Coreia do Sul estabeleceu de forma unilateral o sistema Zona de Identificação de Defesa Aérea KADIZ e que a Rússia realiza sobrevoos como esse de maneira rotineira e respeitando as leis internacionais.

articles.title: Chuva no RS: Enxurradas atingem Garruchos e Cruz Alta; veja alertas | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil emitiu alerta por Cell Broadcast para Garruchos, Soledade e Cruz Alta com risco muito alto de alagamentos e cheias em arroios.
articles.summary: Chuva no Rio Grande do Sul provoca enxurradas em Garruchos, bloqueia a RS-342 em Cruz Alta e mobiliza Defesa Civil com alertas de perigo para todo o estado.
articles.body:
Uma enxurrada atingiu Garruchos , no Noroeste do Rio Grande do Sul, na manhã desta terça-feira (24) e causou danos em estradas, alagou terrenos e chegou a bloquear a entrada do município. Em Cruz Alta , a chuva acumulou cerca de 65 milímetros e atingiu um trecho da RS-342.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, a chuva forte em Garruchos ocorreu entre 6h40 e 8h20. Algumas estradas foram muito afetadas pela força da água. A entrada do município chegou a ser interditada após a elevação do Arroio Lajeado. Os moradores também ficaram sem energia elétrica durante um breve período, mas o fornecimento já foi normalizado.

🚫 A orientação é evitar áreas inundáveis e permanecer em local seguro. Em caso de emergência, os moradores devem acionar a Brigada Militar pelo telefone 190 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193. Segundo a Defesa Civil, eletroeletrônicos devem ser retirados da tomada durante os temporais. Portas e janelas precisam permanecer fechadas, e os animais domésticos devem ser abrigados.

⚠️ Em caso de enxurrada, a orientação é colocar documentos e objetos de valor em sacos plásticos. Se a situação de grande perigo for confirmada, os moradores devem procurar abrigo e evitar permanecer ao ar livre.

Em Cruz Alta, imagens mostram a situação da RS-342 (veja acima) , no trecho entre Cruz Alta e Ijuí, entre os quilômetros 137 e 139. Segundo a prefeitura, foram registrados cerca de 65 milímetros de chuva. Apesar do volume acumulado em um curto período, não houve registro de danos em casas ou de moradores afetados.

As cidades receberam alertas severos por Cell Broadcast pela Defesa Civil, indicando risco muito alto de alagamentos e cheias em arroios devido à chuva volumosa.

O Inmet mantém os três avisos durante toda esta terça-feira . O alerta de perigo potencial abrange todo o estado e prevê chuva de 20 a 30 milímetros por hora ou até 50 milímetros por dia, ventos entre 40 e 60 km/h e possibilidade de granizo.

O aviso de grande perigo atinge áreas da Serra, do Noroeste, do Nordeste e do Norte. Além da chuva e dos ventos acima de 100 km/h , há grande risco de danos em edificações, falta de energia elétrica, perdas em plantações, queda de árvores, alagamentos e transtornos no transporte rodoviário.

articles.title: Incêndio em Oiapoque: fogo em lixão é controlado após um mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura do município emitiu alerta em 26 de outubro devido à fumaça provocada pelo incêndio na lixeira pública. Terraplanagem da área foi uma das medidas adotadas para controlar o fogo.
articles.summary: Bombeiros controlam fogo no lixão de Oiapoque após um mês, mas fumaça de queimadas em terras indígenas e áreas próximas ainda afeta a saúde da população local.
articles.body:
Após quase um mês de incêndio intenso na lixeira pública de Oiapoque , no Norte do Amapá, o Corpo de Bombeiros informou que o fogo foi controlado no local. Apesar disso, a fumaça de outras queimadas ainda encobre a cidade e afeta os moradores.

Em 26 de outubro, a Defesa Civil municipal emitiu alerta após uma densa nuvem de fumaça atingir bairros próximos. A principal preocupação era com os impactos à saúde da população.

Desde então, o cenário se agravou. Além do fogo no lixão, outras queimadas foram registradas, o que levou o município a decretar situação de emergência.

Uma das principais frentes de atuação das equipes ocorreu na área de descarte de resíduos, devido à alta toxicidade da fumaça gerada pelo lixo.

O tenente Clauber Monteiro, do Corpo de Bombeiros, explica que os trabalhos foram divididos em etapas: além do combate com água, houve serviço de terraplanagem para abafar o fogo.

"Foi feito um trabalho de terraplanagem no lixão. Hoje as máquinas se encontram lá fazendo esse serviço até que seja liberado o recurso federal que veio destinado ao lixão", explicou.

Maquinas trabalham na desobstrução do lixão — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo o militar, não há mais focos ativos na lixeira, mas o entorno ainda registra pontos de calor.

"A fumaça continua, de uma maneira menos espessa, mas é em torno do lixão. Hoje o fogo está controlado, os focos de incêndio estão no entorno dele, mas na área onde estava saindo aquela fumaça tóxica que estava prejudicando a população de Oiapoque , já não existe mais", disse.

A extensão da área afetada dificultou o combate às chamas e, segundo a Defesa Civil, o descarte contínuo de resíduos também contribuiu para manter o fogo ativo.

Combate à fumaça em Oiapoque após incêndio em lixão. — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

Uma das medidas estudadas para prevenir novos incêndios no local é o revestimento do solo com argila. A ideia é que a umidade do material abafe os focos de calor e reduza a entrada de oxigênio entre as frestas do lixo.

O projeto depende da contratação de uma empresa especializada e da liberação de verbas federais.

Além disso, a crise acelerou a busca por uma nova área para desativar o espaço, alvo de um impasse judicial que se arrasta há mais de duas décadas.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Oiapoque , a transferência do lixão e a recuperação ambiental do terreno atual atendem a uma decisão definitiva da Justiça — com sentença transitada em julgado

A força-tarefa para solucionar os problemas ambientais e de saúde pública na área conta com o apoio do governo do estado, da Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente (Sema), da Companhia de Desenvolvimento dos Vales do São Francisco e do Parnaíba (Codevasf) e da Universidade Federal do Amapá (Unifap).

Após fumaça tóxica atingir casas, Oiapoque estuda novo terreno para transferir lixão. — Foto: Girlane Duarte/Rede Amazônica

Outra preocupação é o avanço do fogo sobre as terras indígenas de Oiapoque . As regiões de Uaçá e Juminã enfrentam um período crítico, e a fumaça produzida pela queima da vegetação se espalha pela área urbana.

"Essa fumaça que contribui e culmina com a lixeira pública vem das reservas indígenas, os focos estão concentrados mais nas terras indígenas que são terras de difícil acesso", afirmou o tenente.

Um dos principais obstáculos para as equipes é chegar a esses pontos, localizados em áreas de floresta densa. Para definir se a atuação será por via aérea, terrestre ou fluvial, os órgãos planejam sobrevoos de reconhecimento.

Uma Sala de Situação também foi instalada na Aldeia do Manga para monitorar os focos. O combate reúne agentes do Corpo de Bombeiros, do Centro Nacional de Prevenção e Combate aos Incêndios Florestais (Prevfogo) e do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama).

articles.title: Black Friday: como identificar sites falsos e evitar golpes | G1
articles.standfirst: Golpistas usam promoções com prazo limitado e até anúncios patrocinados para atrair consumidores. Conferir o endereço oficial da loja é um dos principais cuidados antes de pagar.
articles.summary: Proteja-se de golpes na Black Friday ao identificar anúncios falsos, conferir a URL oficial da loja e desconfiar de ofertas urgentes com preços abaixo do mercado.
articles.body:
Você encontra o produto que tanto queria pela metade do preço, mas o anúncio diz que a oferta acaba em 30 segundos. Você arriscaria? Antes de pagar, vale conferir se você está mesmo no site oficial da loja.

Essa pressa pode fazer parte do golpe. Sites falsos usam contagens regressivas e avisos de "últimas unidades" para pressionar você a comprar sem pensar duas vezes.

Antes de clicar em uma oferta, confira o endereço do site. O cuidado também vale para anúncios patrocinados nas redes sociais e nos resultados de busca, já que golpistas podem pagar para divulgar páginas falsas.

articles.title: Qualidade do ar em Manaus: Fumaça encobre a Ponte Rio Negro | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital amazonense registrou o ar mais poluído do país nesta terça-feira (24). O índice atingiu nível insalubre, influenciado por queimadas no Amazonas e no Pará.
articles.summary: A qualidade do ar em Manaus atingiu nível insalubre nesta terça-feira devido a queimadas, deixando a Ponte Rio Negro sob fumaça e suspendendo aulas no interior.
articles.body:
Um vídeo enviado ao g1 por Marcel Motta mostra a Ponte Jornalista Phelippe Daou, conhecida como Ponte Rio Negro, encoberta por fumaça durante a travessia entre Manaus e Iranduba , na Região Metropolitana. Nas imagens, um dos pontos mais conhecidos da capital aparece parcialmente encoberto. Ao fundo, o sol também fica escondido pela fumaça.

O registro foi feito nesta terça-feira (24), em meio à piora da qualidade do ar na capital amazonense . Segundo a Prefeitura de Manaus, a condição é influenciada pela fumaça de queimadas em áreas do Amazonas e do Pará , transportada pelos ventos em direção à cidade. A baixa intensidade dos ventos também contribui para a concentração de partículas no ar.

Por volta das 6h, Manaus tinha o ar mais poluído do Brasil , segundo o ranking em tempo real da plataforma internacional IQAir. O Índice de Qualidade do Ar (AQI⁺) chegou a 167, nível classificado como "insalubre" .

O monitoramento do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas ( UEA ), também apontou concentrações elevadas de poluentes em diferentes zonas da cidade. A concentração de partículas finas (PM2.5) em Manaus chegou a 77,9 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³), segundo a IQAir.

O pior índice na capital foi registrado no bairro Puraquequara, na Zona Leste, com 131 µg/m³. Em seguida aparecem Morro da Liberdade (118,1 µg/m³) e Petrópolis (115,6 µg/m³), ambos na Zona Sul.

Na Zona Norte, a Cidade Nova atingiu 112,3 µg/m³, enquanto o Tarumã, na Zona Oeste, marcou 109,1 µg/m³.

🔎 A qualidade do ar é considerada boa pelo sistema Selva quando a concentração de partículas fica entre 0 e 25 µg/m³ . Acima desse valor, a classificação varia de moderada a péssima, conforme a quantidade de poluentes no ar.

Interior do Amazonas tem índices ainda mais críticos

Além da capital, municípios do interior do Amazonas registram níveis péssimos de qualidade do ar por causa da fumaça de queimadas. Em Parintins , por exemplo, a prefeitura informou que a fumaça é provocada por queimadas florestais na região .

Por causa da situação, as aulas da rede municipal foram suspensas novamente na segunda-feira (23) e nesta terça-feira (24). O nível de poluição na cidade chegou a 353,1 µg/m³, segundo o monitoramento do Selva.

Na manhã desta terça-feira, o pior cenário foi registrado em Barreirinha , também no Baixo Amazonas. A concentração de poluentes chegou a 425 µg/m³, índice 17 vezes acima do limite considerado seguro .

Outros municípios do interior também apresentavam índices críticos nas primeiras horas do dia:

Orientações para população se proteger da fumaça

A Defesa Civil de Manaus orienta a população a manter a hidratação, evitar atividades físicas ao ar livre, usar máscara PFF2 em caso de exposição à fumaça e acompanhar os alertas oficiais. Crianças, idosos, gestantes e pessoas com doenças respiratórias devem redobrar os cuidados.

A exposição à fumaça pode provocar tosse, falta de ar, irritação nos olhos e outros sintomas respiratórios.

articles.title: Grupo DB oferece descontos de até 30% em Feirão de Dívidas do Procon | G1
articles.body:
O evento acontecerá das 9h às 14h, no espaço de eventos do Shopping Phelippe Daou, no bairro Cidade de Deus, zona Norte da capital — Foto: Divulgação

Clientes do Cartão DB com débitos em atraso terão a oportunidade de regularizar suas pendências com condições especiais durante a 4ª edição do Feirão de Negociação de Dívidas – Negocia Manaus , que será realizado de 23 a 27 de novembro pelo Procon Manaus. Entre os benefícios oferecidos pelo Grupo DB estão descontos de até 30% sobre o saldo devedor, abatimento de até 100% dos encargos, parcelamento em até 18 vezes e possibilidade de recuperar o crédito após a liquidação do acordo.

As condições variam conforme o tempo de atraso da dívida. Para débitos entre 66 e 150 dias, será possível obter até 100% de desconto nos encargos. Já para pendências acima de 150 dias, os descontos sobre o saldo devedor vão de 10% a 30%. A negociação terá entrada de 10% do valor acordado, com mínimo de R$ 50, e parcelamento em até 18 vezes.

Segundo Gabriel Pedrosa, diretor de Marketing e Expansão do Grupo DB, a participação no evento representa uma oportunidade de ajudar os consumidores a reorganizar a vida financeira ainda neste final de ano. “Queremos proporcionar aos nossos clientes uma oportunidade real de regularizar suas pendências, recuperar o crédito e voltar a contar com os benefícios do Cartão DB. São condições especiais, pensadas para facilitar a negociação e tornar esse retorno ao crédito mais acessível” , destaca.

Além das negociações, o Grupo DB também disponibilizará representantes do setor de Recursos Humanos (RH) para divulgar vagas em diferentes áreas da rede de supermercados e atender pessoas interessadas em oportunidades de trabalho. “Entendemos que cuidar das pessoas também significa oferecer caminhos para recomeçar. Por isso, além de contribuir para que os clientes recuperem seu crédito, estaremos divulgando oportunidades de trabalho. É uma forma de participar de uma iniciativa que pode gerar impactos positivos na vida de muitas famílias” , afirma Gabriel Pedrosa.

O 4ª Feirão de Negociação de Dívidas – Negocia Manaus reúne empresas e consumidores em busca de soluções para regularização de débitos, recuperação do crédito e novas oportunidades profissionais. O evento acontecerá das 9h às 14h, no espaço de eventos da Secretaria Municipal do Trabalho, Empreendedorismo e Inovação (Semtepi), localizado no Shopping Phelippe Daou, no bairro Cidade de Deus, zona Norte da capital.

articles.title: A queda de braço entre governo e mercado financeiro - O Assunto #1851 | G1
articles.standfirst: Enquanto os índices econômicos derrapam – nesta segunda (23), o dólar chegou a bater a marca de R$ 6 e fechou o dia em R$ 5,93 – o governo apresenta seu pacote de medidas fiscais.
articles.summary: Enquanto os índices econômicos derrapam – nesta segunda (23), o dólar chegou a bater a marca de R$ 6 e fechou o dia em R$ 5,93 – o governo apresenta seu pacote de medidas fiscais.
articles.body:
Neste último sábado (21), o presidente Lula disse em uma live que "foi o presidente que mais fez superávit primário neste país" e que "não é o sistema financeiro que vai ensinar a dirigir o país". As declarações são reações ao discurso de parte da Faria Lima de que seu governo não quer – ou não consegue – equilibrar as contas públicas. Enquanto os índices econômicos derrapam – nesta segunda-feira (23), o dólar chegou a bater a marca de R$ 6 e fechou o dia em R$ 5,92 – o governo apresenta seu pacote de medidas fiscais, que ganhou o apelido de "Plano Moretti", em referência ao ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti, que idealizou a proposta que prevê economia de R$ 50 bilhões em 2027. O texto, que já havia sido aprovado no Senado, foi chancelado pela Câmara também nesta segunda-feira.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery recebe o economista Felipe Salto. Na entrevista, Salto pondera os exageros do mercado financeiro com a necessidade da apresentação de uma proposta crível para a trajetória da dívida brasileira. O economista também explica por que o cenário de instabilidade internacional reflete na desvalorização do real diante do dólar.

Convidado: Felipe Salto, economista-chefe e sócio da Warren Investimentos, professor de Finanças Públicas do IDP e ex-secretário da Fazenda e do Planejamento do Estado de São Paulo e ex-diretor-executivo da Instituição Fiscal Independente (IFI).

O podcast O Assunto é produzido por: Luiz Felipe Silva, Luiz Gabriel Franco, Juliene Moretti, Stéphanie Nascimento, Marco Antônio Martins e Thomé Granemann. Na apresentação: Natuza Nery.

O Assunto é o podcast diário produzido pelo g1, disponível em todas as plataformas de áudio e no YouTube. Desde a estreia, em agosto de 2019, o podcast O Assunto soma mais de 168 milhões de downloads em todas as plataformas de áudio.

articles.title: Falta de água em Passo de Camaragibe: moradores bloqueiam a AL-101 | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura diz que problema acontece devido a deficiência na rede elétrica do local, que acaba queimando as bombas que puxam água dos poços artesianos. Equatorial apura o caso.
articles.summary: Devido à falta de água em Passo de Camaragibe, moradores bloqueiam a AL-101 com fogo em protesto contra a queima constante de bombas na rede de abastecimento local.
articles.body:
Moradores realizam manifestação contra falta de água e fecham trecho de rodovia em Passo de Camaragibe — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Moradores de Passo de Camaragibe realizam, nesta terça-feira (24), um protesto contra a falta de água no município. Os manifestantes bloquearam os dois sentidos de um trecho da AL-101, próximo ao povoado Bom Despacho.

De acordo com os manifestantes, o problema no abastecimento de água na região persiste há dias. Os moradores atearam fogo em troncos de madeira para impedir a circulação de veículos.

Devido ao protesto, o trânsito na região está intenso. Segundo os moradores, apenas veículos de emergência, como ambulâncias e viaturas, têm passagem liberada.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Verde Alagoas, responsável por parte da distribuição de água no município, e foi informado de que o problema está relacionado à operação dos poços artesianos, que são geridos pela prefeitura.

Ao g1 , a Prefeitura de Passo de Camaragibe informou que o problema ocorre devido à instabilidade na rede elétrica do local , que, segundo o órgão, é fraca. Por conta disso, as bombas utilizadas para puxar água dos poços acabam queimando.

A prefeitura informou ainda que as equipes acompanham o protesto e estão à disposição para solucionar o problema o mais rápido possível.

A reportagem também procurou a Equatorial Alagoas, que informou estar apurando o caso.

articles.body: LAKHISARAI: At least five people, including two women and a child, were killed and three others injured after an SUV collided head-on with a truck in Bihar's Lakhisarai district early Tuesday morning, police said.The accident took place near Gunsagar village under the Tetarhat police station area on the Lakhisarai-Jamui main road.The deceased included two women, a child and two men, one of whom was driving the SUV. articles.title: Google responds to 'huge layoffs' in India report; says: Last week Google Cloud made …
articles.summary: Google has denied reports of widespread layoffs in India.
articles.body: Google has denied reports of widespread layoffs in India. The company addressed the claims on Tuesday, November 24, after X user Venkatesh Alla wrote, “Huge layoffs at Google India. What's going on?” His question followed an anonymous post on the professional forum Blind about alleged job cuts and termination notices. The official Google Cloud India account replied directly to Alla’s post and wrote: “These rumors are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organizational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritization of work.”​The company’s response gave a figure for the roles eliminated in its India cloud division. However, it did not identify the teams affected or say where the roles were based. Google Cloud India even posted the same response under several other posts about the claims.​Google Cloud layoffs in India: What were the rumours aboutIn a post, the anonymous poster described themselves as a level-four employee in Bengaluru and said they had come across several discussions in Google’s channel on Blind. They linked to two threads and described what they had read about cuts in India-based cloud teams, severance offers and potential changes in January.​The post claimed that people are posting about sudden cuts across India Cloud teams, with zero link to performance and while their US counterparts weren't touched. Others are getting 24-hour "resign or get fired" ultimatums with just 1 month severance, impossible pre-PIPs that block internal transfers, and rumours of January VEPs or layoffs in P&D.​The claims about termination deadlines, severance and possible January cuts remain unverified. The person who shared the post on Blind even asked whether the changes were confined to Google’s cloud and developer relations teams or signalled a broader slowdown in hiring in India. Google’s reply addressed the cloud reorganisation and gave no details about hiring plans or future cuts. After the company replied, Alla wrote, “Pre-Prioritization?....Wow....”​The Blind user further said the authors of the two linked threads had deleted them. In an edit, the person wrote, “Google has also shared its response, but I’ll leave it to everyone to decide whether they find it convincing. I shared what I came across because I believe it’s worth discussing, and I stand by bringing the conversation here!”​​Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Pennsylvania reports ninth measles death in ongoing state outbreak
articles.summary: CDC and state figures on measles deaths differ as Pennsylvania faces an escalating health crisis in 46 counties.
articles.body:
Pennsylvania health officials have reported another death linked to the ongoing measles outbreak, bringing the state’s death toll associated with the highly contagious viral disease to nine.

The state Department of Health confirmed on Monday the death of an unvaccinated resident of Centre County in central ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Pennsylvania who tested positive for measles.

Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, has recorded 1,638 confirmed measles cases across 46 counties so far in 2026, including 330 hospitalisations.

The nine deaths were recorded across five counties, as Lancaster County accounted ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌for three deaths, while Jefferson County reported two.

Virginia recorded its first measles-related death in more than three decades on Friday, just days after the United States lost its hard-fought designation as having eliminated the highly contagious virus.

Meanwhile, Wisconsin has reported two deaths, and New York state has recorded one child death linked to the disease.

However, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported only six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, without specifying the ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠states where the deaths were recorded.

The discrepancy between state and federal tolls emerged earlier this year after the health agency, under US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures .

The US Department of Health and Human Services said it ⁠⁠⁠⁠was “saddened to hear of another death in Pennsylvania”, adding that the CDC has provided the state with nearly $4m in one-time emergency funding for ⁠⁠⁠⁠response efforts in 2027.

A total of 5,838 measles cases were confirmed across the country this year as of November 19, according to CDC data . The figure is the highest number reported by the CDC since 1991.

Children below the age of five account for 18 percent of cases, while children between the ages of five and 19 make up 41 percent of cases.

The number of confirmed cases in November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed measles cases reported for the full year of 2025.

articles.title: Saurav Das: Cockroach Janta Party leader says he was stopped from flying to UK for Oxford event
articles.summary: Saurav Das said that immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him that his passport had been "flagged".
articles.body:
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.

Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".

It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests , said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.

He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.

"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," Das wrote on X.

A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.

On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.

"The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country," she wrote.

Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.

In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .

In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands of people detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.

The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.

There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.

In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.

In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

articles.body: Brian Stacey, known to his family and friends as Bunny, experienced a serious decline in his health following an incident over the Christmas period in late 2024. He lost much of his ability to move around and developed difficulties eating and swallowing. He eventually needed a feeding tube for nutrition and became dependent on others for daily care. His condition showed little sign of improvement, and after discussions with his family, it was decided that he should receive end-of-life care. He was admitted to Hatherleigh Nursing Home in Devon in January 2025.According to Evolve Care Group, Bunny's condition gradually improved after his admission. With support from nursing home staff and physiotherapists, he regained much of his mobility and independence and learnt to walk again with a stick.How Bunny's family life took a turn after his health deterioratedBunny had spent his life in Devon, where he was born and raised in Merton. He worked in practical roles, from sawmills to maintenance and gardening at Clinton Estates, for 50 years. He married Julie in 1974, and they have two children, Michelle and Kevin, as well as a grandson, Tyler.His interests included classic cars, particularly his BMW 635 CSi, and watching television with a cup of black Twinings Earl Grey tea. Towards the end of 2024, his circumstances changed after he suffered a fall over the Christmas period. His health subsequently deteriorated, beginning a difficult period for him and his family.Bunny's declining health led to end-of-life care at a Devon nursing homeDuring his hospital stay, Bunny became increasingly dependent on others for tasks he had previously managed himself. His mobility declined significantly, and he developed serious difficulties eating and swallowing. He eventually needed a feeding tube to receive nutrition. Despite medical care, his condition remained poor, with little sign of improvement.Discussions were held with his family about what would be best for him, and the decision was eventually made to focus on keeping him comfortable through end-of-life care. Bunny arrived at Hatherleigh Nursing Home in January 2025. His health had changed dramatically in a short period, leaving both him and his family uncertain about what would happen in the weeks ahead.Care staff and therapists helped Bunny regain his mobility and independenceIn the weeks after his arrival, Bunny began showing signs of recovery, despite initially having little expectation of improvement. Nursing and care staff worked with external multidisciplinary teams to help him regain some of his independence. One major change involved his eating and drinking. After previously needing a feeding tube, he gradually began taking food and drink by mouth.Speech and language therapists reviewed his needs as he improved. He later returned to sitting at the dining table, drinking independently and enjoying meals with some assistance. Physiotherapists and care team members also supported his mobility. By October 2026, he could walk independently using a frame and had progressed to walking with a stick.Bunny gradually regained control over his everyday routineBunny's progress has also helped him take a more active role in decisions about his daily life. When he first arrived, his cognitive ability had declined alongside his health, so some decisions had to be made in his best interests. As his condition improved, he became increasingly able to communicate his preferences.He could choose what he wanted for breakfast and talk with staff about his day. On one occasion, he said he had enjoyed spending an afternoon upstairs because it was calm and quiet. More than a year and a half after his arrival, he still needs support but has regained much of his independence.Disclaimer: This article is based on information shared by Evolve Care Group about Brian Stacey’s recovery at Hatherleigh Nursing Home. articles.title: Man's shock at Ryanair flight to Spain using wife's passport
articles.summary: Ben Moore says he is still baffled over how he was able to make the journey without being stopped.
articles.body:
A man who mistakenly travelled to Spain using his wife's passport has said he is still baffled about how he was able to make the trip without being stopped in the UK.

Ben Moore, from Talke, in Staffordshire, noticed there was a problem soon after getting off his Ryanair flight while he was queuing to get his passport checked at Alicante airport.

"I opened up the passport there and, to my horror, it was my wife's photo on the passport," he said. "The lads who I was with basically said the colour drained out of me immediately."

Third-party provider Swissport, which carries out Ryanair's checks at Manchester Airport where Moore flew from, said it was now reinforcing mandatory boarding procedures.

Moore, who was travelling to Alicante on a stag party with friends, told BBC Radio Stoke he initially thought he must have picked up his wife's passport in addition to his own.

He said he approached Spanish police who - along with the language barrier - appeared to be as confused as he was about how he had turned up there without his own passport.

"I searched through all my luggage about eight times thinking there's no way I could have got to Alicante without my own passport," he said.

"They could not believe that I'd got to Spain on my wife's passport."

Moore added that he was "treated a bit like a criminal," and had found their handling of the situation "a little bit intimidating".

He owns a property in Spain and said he did the journey a number of times each year.

On this occasion, however, his trip ended with him being returned to the UK while his friends continued their holiday without him.

Manchester Airport said the responsibility for checking passports was with the airlines and that airports only needed boarding cards from passengers when they are passing through security.

The Department for Transport confirmed it was the responsibility of airlines to check passports, as part of the check-in and boarding process.

It added that passengers were screened for security purposes before boarding an aircraft.

A spokesperson for Swissport UK & Ireland said: "We take our document verification and security responsibilities extremely seriously.

"We are carrying out a full internal review into this incident and are actively reinforcing mandatory boarding check procedures with our operational teams."

articles.title: Delia Smith joins campaigners against £1.2bn Keswick data centre
articles.summary: The TV cook and author is worried about the environmental impact of the proposed Keswick facility.
articles.body:
Television cook Delia Smith has joined opponents of a £1.2bn data centre, arguing it would threaten a nature reserve.

Campaigners fear the proposed centre at Keswick, on the edge of Norwich, will create noise pollution and have a negative impact on nearby Marston Marsh.

Smith, honorary life president and former majority shareholder of Norwich City FC, said: "I love Norfolk. You can't be involved in a football club for 55 years without being attached to the people and the beauty of Norfolk. I feel very strongly about it."

But developer Norwich Apex said an ecological impact assessment concluded no effect on the reserve was expected.

Data centres are facilities that store and process vast amounts of data and run the software and online services used by millions of people.

This centre, off the A140 Ipswich Road, would need 150 MW of power to run and would feature 72 chiller units on its roof.

According to planning documents, the building would be about 20m (65ft) high.

A planning application for the centre has been lodged with South Norfolk Council.

If approved, construction could begin at the end of 2027 and it would be operational by 2028.

The plans have emerged at the same time as a much bigger proposal for a data centre and solar farm elsewhere in Norfolk, south of King's Lynn, which would require more than five times as much electricity.

What are data centres and are more coming to the East?

The developer has said the Keswick facility would use " air-cooling technology " and not require water for cooling.

But Smith, who lives in Suffolk, said: "We haven't got enough water, and data centres use an awful lot of water.

""It's one of the biggest [data centres] and It doesn't do anything for the Norfolk community. Where is the £1.2bn coming from? And who are the people who are going to presumably make money out of it?

"It's not going to do anything for the local community, it's the opposite. It's going to be bad."

It is hoped the centre will harness wind energy by connecting to the Hornsea 3 substation nearby.

Smith said: "Renewable energy is going into the grid but it doesn't supply everything now.

"What are you going to do when you have this huge data centre absolutely sucking up energy?"

Other opponents of the plan include broadcaster and entrepreneur Jake Humphrey .

Other campaigners include Matt Tomlinson of Yare Valley Meadow Makers, who believes the development will have a "disastrous effect" on nocturnal wildlife.

"On this Marston Marsh site we have nine protected bat species, we have three different owl species and these will all need the quiet conditions to effectively hunt," he said.

"I think this is an awful idea; awful for the wildlife and awful for the people."

In recent days, Labour MP for South Norfolk, Ben Goldsborough, who believes the development would be in the wrong place , has been appointed to a new data centre committee that will scrutinise the government's national policies.

Matt Bartram, chief executive of Norwich Apex, said: "Our ambition is to deliver one of the UK's greenest data centres, using low-carbon power supplied via Norwich Main substation. Protecting nearby ecological sites, including Marston Marshes has shaped the design from the outset.

"Detailed environment assessments have informed our plans to reduce noise and screen the development from view.

"We propose planting more than 15,700 trees and over 1.7km of new hedgerow, with the plans delivering a 13% biodiversity net gain."

Correction 24 November 2026: This article was amended to clarify the size of this data centre in comparison to other planned developments and to make clear the developer's position on water usage.

articles.title: Malaysia set to return thousands of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.summary: The announcement comes five days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
articles.body:
Malaysia will send more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar in a new round of repatriations, said Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

The announcement on Tuesday comes five days after the International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled that Myanmar’s security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya minority .

Malaysia has historically offered safe haven to exiles from Myanmar but has grown increasingly frustrated by large numbers of refugees, saying that hosting them has become a financial burden and security risk.

In late September, around 1,500 migrants were sent back to war-torn Myanmar in an opaque scheme that concerns rights groups.

Addressing the Malaysian parliament, Anwar said 1,500 Myanmar nationals will be returned on three navy ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠vessels from December 6 to 7. “For the month of December, 5,303 will be brought back by aircraft at the expense of the Myanmar government,” he said.

As of August, there were 225,740 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UNHCR in Malaysia, around 90 percent of them from Myanmar, according to the agency’s data.

The UN’s highest court ruled last week that Myanmar authorities must “allow and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return” of refugees displaced either within Myanmar or abroad.

Malaysia hosted Myanmar’s former junta chief-turned-President Min Aung Hlaing last ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠month, despite criticisms from rights groups that the move risked legitimising Myanmar’s government and posed dangers for those being returned.

Anwar said his engagements with Myanmar’s former leader were part ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠of efforts to safeguard Malaysia’s interests and in line with the ruling by the International Court of Justice, which was “to guarantee a safe and dignified return” for those fleeing persecution.

The PM acknowledged that many asylum seekers in Malaysia were “victims of atrocities carried out by the Myanmar regime”, but said Malaysia could no longer afford to ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌host refugees and that hoping for them to be resettled in third countries had not worked.

Late last month, Malaysia said it would seek clarification from Myanmar about reports that hundreds of migrants recently returned to the country were being held in military detention.

Anwar did not mention the request for clarification, but said Malaysia reiterated its stance over concerns about the Rohingya and other ethnic groups, which was also underscored by the ICJ’s ruling.

The mainly Muslim Rohingya – described as the ‘world’s most persecuted minority’ – make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the United Nations.

articles.title: US army says detonation of lead explosives in Iowa will proceed Wednesday
articles.summary: Public outcry led to a legal battle when details of the plans to conduct two controlled detonations surfaced.
articles.body:
The United States military will proceed with its plan on Wednesday to blow up a deteriorating stockpile of toxic lead explosives in rural Iowa, according to the army’s top civilian official, after a federal appeals court gave clearance to the waste disposal operation.

In an announcement late Monday on X, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle called the choice to move forward a “consensus decision” among all the federal agencies involved, as well as the courts and state officials.

“Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa’s current and incoming governors say the call belongs to the experts,” Telle said.

“We are proceeding with the controlled removal in full coordination with all state, local and federal authorities.”

On Monday, the incoming Democratic governor of Iowa Rob Sands said authorities should proceed based on assessments by experts on the ground.

But Sands also called for more transparency and the disclosure of information he had been briefed on as the incoming governor.

“The Administration should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks,” Sands wrote in a post on X. “Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward.”

The Army prompted a public outcry last week when details surfaced of its plan to conduct two controlled detonations of 68 drums containing almost 4,500kg (10,000lb) of degraded lead azide, a chemical used in munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa.

Environmental groups immediately filed suit to block the plan, raising public safety concerns over the likelihood that the explosions would release a plume of toxic lead dust over homes, crops and livestock far beyond the detonation site, about 240km (150 miles) southeast of Des Moines.

The lawsuit challenged a special permit granted for the operation by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

The EPA countered that a managed detonation would be far less risky than an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion of the highly volatile material, a scenario the agency said was growing more likely as the weather turns colder in Iowa.

According to the EPA, any attempt to chemically neutralise or relocate the storage drums would also risk an uncontrolled blast.

A three-judge panel of the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals last Thursday issued a temporary stay blocking the EPA’s permit while the court more thoroughly reviewed the case.

But Trump administration lawyers filed a legal notice two days later asserting that the Army intended to carry out the controlled detonation with or without court approval, citing an emergency exemption to federal environmental laws.

Then, in another twist on Monday, US President Donald Trump weighed in on the controversy, ordering the Army to hold off on its disposal plan until the appeals court had ruled in its favour.

Hours after Trump’s edict on Monday pausing the army’s demolition plan, the 8th Circuit sided with the EPA and lifted the court’s earlier stay, removing the final legal obstacle. But the status of the detonation plan remained unclear until Telle’s announcement on Monday night.

articles.title: In 2020, lineman Josh Smith quit his job to build Montana Knife Company from his garage; four years later, it reached $50 million in revenue, and by 2026 it had about 125 employees
articles.summary: Discover how Josh Smith turned Montana Knife Company from a humble garage startup into a $50 million business in just four years, employing 125 people and specializing in high-quality, American-made knives.
articles.body: It took Josh Smith several years to hone his craft of bladesmithing while being employed as a union journeyman power lineman. In that period of time, he made custom knives in his garage in Frenchtown, Montana, where he managed to sell some of his work for $4,000 to $5,000. At that time, he started thinking about whether he could transform his knife-making into a more serious business where he would provide clients with high-quality American-made knives without spending thousands of dollars on customized products. In 2020, Smith resigned from his position as a union journeyman power lineman to fully concentrate on his company, Montana Knife Company. In four years' time, the company achieved a revenue of $50 million and grew up to 125 employees, according to Fortune.Josh Smith learned knife-making as a childInterest in knife-making developed at the age of 11. Smith received a knife from his Little League baseball coach as a gift during Christmas. The coach allowed Smith into the workshop, where he acquainted him with the art of knife-making. Smith started accumulating money to purchase tools from minor tasks, such as lawn mowing and working in the family excavation firm. Smith practised bladesmithing through his school years and Fortune reported he reached master bladesmith status at 19. Smith attained the rank of master bladesmith, set to be the youngest in the world at that time. Smith also registered the name Montana Knife Company when he was 19 years old. But did not start the company until 2020, when he was 39.The company started in a two-car garageThe development of Montana Knife Company started in 2020 in Smith’s two-car garage in Frenchtown. The knife parts were manufactured through cooperation with machine shops in different states and assembled by him. Smith was helped by his wife, Jessica and children, especially on weekends. On December 30, 2020, Smith quit his lineman position to focus only on the business. The first employee of the company, Tristan Richter, joined the company at the beginning of its operations.Tristan assisted in assembly, sharpening and delivery. Smith and his team set a sales goal of $100,000 for 2021. However, the company made almost $1.9 million in revenue, as shown in company documents examined by Fortune. At the end of that year, there were five employees in the company. With the increase in orders, Smith decided to build a 10,000-square-foot facility in the horse pasture near his house. According to Fortune, the company moved into the building on January 1, 2023, with 11 employees.Montana Knife Company reached $50 million in revenueThe growth of the company persisted as more people began purchasing the hunting and outdoor knives manufactured by the company. Due to the manufacturing of knives in America and the practical nature of the designs, the company succeeded in having customers from outside Montana. Fortune's May 23, 2026 profile of Smith, written by Nick Lichtenberg, reported that Montana Knife Company earned $50 million in sales four years after its launch. The company later moved to a 51,000-square-foot factory in Missoula.Its workforce expanded alongside its manufacturing operations. In November 2024, the Montana Department of Commerce reported that the company had 70 employees and planned to add 100 more jobs over the following couple of years. According to the Missoula Economic Partnership, the company unveiled plans for an $18 million expansion that included building the new 50,000-square-foot Missoula factory. The Montana Department of Commerce said $1.5 million in federal funding, through its Small Business Credit Initiative and Automation Loan Participation programs, partially supported the $18 million project. The federal money covered only a portion of the project's total cost. Fortune's Nick Lichtenberg reported in May 2026 that the company employs approximately 125 people. The development of the company from a garage to a manufacturing factory had made the many years that Smith spent making knives worthwhile.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Pakistan petrol pumps threaten nationwide shutdown, give govt 15 days to meet demands
articles.summary: Pakistan's petroleum dealers have threatened to shut down petrol pumps across the country if the government fails to introduce a monthly fuel pricing
articles.body: Pakistan's petroleum dealers have threatened to shut down petrol pumps across the country if the government fails to introduce a monthly fuel pricing mechanism, giving authorities 15 days to address their demands, according to a report by Dawn.The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) said frequent revisions in petroleum prices were causing serious financial difficulties for fuel retailers and rapidly depleting their working capital. The association warned that continued uncertainty could force petrol pumps to suspend operations, potentially triggering a law and order situation.Addressing a presser at the Karachi Press Club, PPDA chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh, along with other association representatives, demanded that dealers' profit margins be raised to 8 per cent of the retail price. They also alleged that refineries had cut petrol and diesel supplies, with one refinery reportedly halting diesel supplies altogether, Dawn reported.The dealers claimed that they collectively contribute PKR 5.74 billion to the national exchequer every day and urged the government to take their financial concerns into account before introducing further changes to petroleum-related policies.Khuda Bakhsh said previous strike threats had been withdrawn following government intervention, but several demands remained unresolved. He argued that changing market conditions following the US-Iran war made it necessary for the authorities to reconsider the existing pricing arrangement, according to Dawn.Pakistan introduced the daily fuel pricing mechanism in July, citing volatility in international oil markets. Under the system, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) announces revised petroleum prices every day.The PPDA has repeatedly opposed the arrangement, demanding a return to monthly or fortnightly price revisions. Earlier, another petroleum dealers' association had also postponed its nationwide strike following assurances from the petroleum minister that the daily pricing system would initially operate on a trial basis.In August, the government approved a 15.5 per cent increase in dealers' margins on petrol and high-speed diesel. The move raised the margin by PKR 1.34 per litre to PKR 9.98, effective September 1. However, the dealers' demand for an 8 per cent margin remains unresolved.You use AI every day.
